subject.title: All LLM API calls time out simultaneously despite APIs being reachable (multi-agent concurrency issue)

question: Should OpenClaw decouple Telegram runner sink concurrency from `agents.defaults.maxConcurrent` for multi-agent Telegram deployments, or keep the shared concurrency model and document/tune the supported operator settings?
rationale: The remaining code-backed gap changes how channel ingress competes with agent turn concurrency, which affects delivery behavior and operator expectations beyond a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Require live repro first
options.body: Capture a current-main four-agent Telegram trace before changing concurrency semantics, then decide based on whether ingress starvation is still present.

options.title: Decouple Telegram ingress concurrency
options.body: Add a Telegram-owned concurrency policy or derived default with live Telegram proof and regression coverage for concurrent agent load.

options.title: Keep shared concurrency
options.body: Leave sink concurrency tied to agent maxConcurrent and improve diagnostics/docs around provider timeout and process-level tuning.

recommendation.title: Require live repro first
recommendation.body: Capture a current-main four-agent Telegram trace before changing concurrency semantics, then decide based on whether ingress starvation is still present.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining decision is closest to the current Telegram monitor concurrency line and recent queue/fallback ownership trail.
